newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli court okays demolition of bomber's home. [CORRECTED 21:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Israeli court okays demolition of bomber's home. [CORRECTED 21:40 GMT]

text.p: Israel's High Court on Sunday rejected an appeal by the family of the Islamist suicide bomber who killed himself and three Israeli women 10 days ago against army demolition of their home in the West Bank.
Court spokesman Moshe Gorali confirmed the three-judge court's rejection of the appeal by a 2-1 vote.
Israeli security sources said it was possible the demolition of the home at Surif village near the West Bank town of Hebron could take place later on Sunday.

On March 21, Mousa Abdel-Qader Ghneimat (corrects to clarify name) blew himself at a Tel Aviv cafe. A caller to Israeli police claimed the Hamas Islamic Resistance Movement was responsible for the attack.
The bombing worsened Israeli-Palestinian relations already in crisis over Israel breaking ground for a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
Clashes in the West Bank between Israeli troops and Palestinians hurling stones entered their 11th day on Sunday. On Saturday, troops killed a Palestinian, the first fatality in the unrest.
Israeli army demolition of the family homes of Palestinians who kill Israelis has been condemned by Palestinians and human rights groups as collective punishment.
